threat_event: Attacker signs in to the hosted SCADA web HMI with the shared operator password and opens feeder reclosers, dropping every member
threat_source: Cybercriminal or hacktivist targeting small utilities
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One shared operator login used by 4 field staff on tablets and phones; no MFA on SCADA; password unchanged 2023 to 2026-07-24; web HMI reachable from any internet connection
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.27(c)(5); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3); DOE-417 (criterion 3)
existing_controls: Password changed 2026-07-24; HMI requires a password; reclosers have local control and lockout on the device
treatment_plan: Named SCADA accounts for each user; MFA on every SCADA login (vendor feature); restrict HMI sign-in to the cooperative's devices; vendor login alerts to the Line Superintendent

threat_event: Attacker reaches a line recloser through an internet-exposed cellular modem and changes protection settings or operates it
threat_source: Opportunistic attacker scanning the internet for exposed devices
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Line recloser modems on public-IP data plans; management page of the LR-4 modem answered from the internet with the installer's default password (found in P07 testing 2026-08-11); no inventory of firmware versions
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.27(c)(5); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Passwords changed on all 6 modems and management ports closed by carrier setting on 2026-08-12
treatment_plan: Move the 6 line recloser modems to the private cellular network used by the substation gateway; OT inventory with firmware versions; firmware review with the recloser vendor

threat_event: Mass remote disconnect sent through the AMI head-end, by a compromised account or a wrong command
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Any of 4 users can send remote disconnect and load-control commands to many meters at once; no second approval; no MFA on the AMI head-end
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.27(c)(7); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Named AMI accounts; 120 of about 820 meters have a disconnect switch
treatment_plan: Ask the AMI vendor to enable MFA and a two-person rule for disconnect commands above 5 meters; remove disconnect rights from users who do not need them; check medical-needs flags before any disconnect

threat_event: Business email compromise diverts the monthly power bill payment (about $53,000) to a fraudster's account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: A 2025 attempt was caught only because the General Manager happened to call the G&T; no written callback rule; no phishing training
regulatory_driver: Internal (payment controls); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: MFA on email; General Manager approves bank changes by habit
treatment_plan: Written callback rule for any change of payee bank details (POL-02 C.7); annual training and quarterly phishing simulations; external-sender email banner

threat_event: Ransomware on an office computer encrypts the synced shared drive and spreads to the operations workstation
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No phishing training; operations workstation not MSP-managed; flat office network; backups not immutable
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.28(c)(4); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: MSP antivirus and patching on the 5 office computers; firewall
treatment_plan: Enroll the operations workstation and tablets in MSP management; MSP-managed EDR; separate network segment for the operations workstation; immutable vault backups

threat_event: Theft of member personal information (Social Security numbers, medical-needs list) from the shared drive or a mailbox
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: About 2,400 scanned membership applications with SSNs in the shared drive; no alerts for mass downloads
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171
existing_controls: MFA on email and the business suite; suite access by role
treatment_plan: Move SSNs into the CIS only and delete the scanned applications after a retention check; mass-download alerts in the productivity suite

threat_event: Recloser or RTU settings cannot be restored after device failure, tampering, or loss of the Line Superintendent's laptop
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Settings live on one laptop; vault copy made by hand, last in February 2026; never restore-tested
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.28(c)(4); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Laptop encrypted; February 2026 copy in the vault
treatment_plan: Settings library in the vault updated after every change; quarterly restore test of one device's settings to a spare control; approved settings printouts in the ERP binder

threat_event: Hosted SCADA vendor outage or compromise stops or misuses SCADA for all of its utility customers
threat_source: Service provider failure or supply chain attack
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor support staff hold standing administrator access to SCADA and the substation gateway; contract has no security terms
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.27(c)(4); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 Type 2 report (reviewed 2026-08-20); local control at every device
treatment_plan: Vendor access to the gateway only on request, logged by the Line Superintendent; contract terms for 24-hour incident notice and named support staff

threat_event: Compromise of the MSP's remote management tool gives attackers access to every office computer
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MSP tool has administrator access to all office computers; no review of MSP security practices
regulatory_driver: Internal (vendor oversight); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: MSP states it uses MFA on its console (not evidenced)
treatment_plan: Annual MSP security review (questionnaire and evidence); 24-hour incident notice in the MSP contract

threat_event: Former employee uses a still-valid shared password to reach SCADA
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared operator password was not changed when a lineworker left in May 2025; no termination checklist
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.27(c)(5); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Password changed 2026-07-24; vendor login history (90 days) showed no unknown sign-ins
treatment_plan: Termination checklist covering SCADA, AMI, suite, email, and keys; named accounts (R-001)

threat_event: Cellular carrier outage removes SCADA, line recloser, AMI collector, and tablet links at once
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One carrier for every field link; no second path
existing_controls: Local control at devices; paper maps; radios in trucks
treatment_plan: Second carrier SIM in the substation gateway; ERP step for posting a lineworker at Substation 1 when SCADA is lost

threat_event: Hurricane damages lines and headquarters while business systems and contacts needed for recovery are not planned for
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: ERP lacks a business continuity section; contact list outdated; one paper copy at the office; no plan for loss of SCADA, AMI, or the business suite
existing_controls: ERP from 2021 exercised each May; standby generator; G&T mutual aid
treatment_plan: ERP update: business continuity section from the BIA, cyber annex, current contacts; copies in every truck and at key staff homes; Board approval

threat_event: RUS loan application is delayed because the General Manager cannot certify a satisfactory VRA and ERP
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: VRA from 2005 with no cyber content; ERP not signed by the current General Manager
existing_controls: 2023 RUS review closed with no open items
treatment_plan: Updated VRA (this register and the P03 rows) by 2026-12-31; ERP update approved by the Board by 2027-01-31; certification letter ready for the 2027 application

threat_event: A cyber event that interrupts service is not reported on Form DOE-417 within 1 hour
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Nobody knew about DOE-417; no agreement with the G&T and the Balancing Authority on who files
regulatory_driver: DOE-417 (criteria 3 and 4); Pub. L. 93-275 sec. 13(b)
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: DOE-417 steps in the P08 runbook; written filing arrangement with the G&T; DOE-417 account set up in advance

threat_event: Staff do not recognize or report a cyber incident, so containment and reporting clocks are missed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident response plan; no reporting rule; no training
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: POL-03 and the P08 runbook; reporting card in every truck and office; annual tabletop

threat_event: Malware on the unmanaged operations workstation or a truck tablet captures SCADA credentials
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Operations workstation and tablets not patched or monitored by the MSP; workstation signs in automatically
regulatory_driver: 7 CFR 1730.27(c)(5); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Tablets use the device's built-in protections
treatment_plan: Enroll in MSP management; remove automatic sign-in; screen lock; tablets under mobile device management

threat_event: AMI vendor uses member interval data from the peak-forecasting trial to train its models or shares it
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Add-on switched on without a review of data-use terms; standard terms allow product-improvement use
regulatory_driver: Internal (member data commitments); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Data stays in the vendor's existing service
treatment_plan: Contract addendum: no training or sharing of member data outside the service, deletion on exit; see P10

threat_event: Peak forecast misses the G&T coincident peak hour, raising the monthly demand charge
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Trial model not validated against the G&T's actual peak hours; no error tracking
regulatory_driver: Internal (wholesale contract costs)
existing_controls: General Manager reviews the G&T peak advisory before each event
treatment_plan: Compare forecasts with the G&T's peak hours monthly; keep human approval of every load-control event (P10)

threat_event: Lost or stolen truck tablet exposes an open SCADA session, maps, and member contact data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Tablets stay signed in to SCADA and the outage module; not under device management
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171; Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Built-in device encryption with a passcode
treatment_plan: Device management with remote wipe; SCADA session timeout; named logins (R-001)

threat_event: Intruder enters Substation 1 and tampers with the RTU, gateway, or recloser controls
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Gate secured by a padlock with untracked keys; no camera; gate opening not alarmed
existing_controls: Fenced and locked; cabinets locked; weekly drive-by
treatment_plan: Re-key with a restricted key and key log; door switch on the control cabinet alarmed to SCADA

threat_event: Staff paste member data or network details into a public generative AI chatbot
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No rule on AI tools before POL-04
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171; Internal
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: POL-04 4.6 prohibits Restricted data in public AI tools; covered in annual training

threat_event: Card data exposed through the cooperative's payment pages
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Payments go only to the processor's hosted page and IVR; no card data in cooperative systems
regulatory_driver: Internal (processor agreement)
existing_controls: Processor-hosted page and IVR
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low; confirm the portal links to the processor page at each annual review

threat_event: Load-control command error leaves enrolled water heaters off for many hours
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Load-control events end by schedule set in the head-end; no check that switches restored
regulatory_driver: Internal (load-control program terms)
existing_controls: Program terms limit events to 4 hours; members can opt out
treatment_plan: Accepted: impact Low (comfort, no safety effect); member complaints go to the Office and Finance Manager
